clue.text: Elevation, but no elevator

parts.note: an elevator is the American word for a lift
off can mean not available, as a dish that is off the menu

explanation.surface: Someone notes there is height to be gained but the building has no elevator.
explanation.walkthrough: Read 'no elevator' as 'the lift is off', with the two pieces swapped into answer order.
explanation.definitionFit: The launch of a rocket is its rise from the ground, an elevation into the air.

clue.text: The dog that is none too steady on its feet

definitions.text: that is none too steady on its feet

explanation.surface: A dog described as being a bit wobbly on its legs.
explanation.definitionFit: A breed of crossbred hunting hound, and also one who staggers or lurches about unsteadily.

clue.text: Verbal conceit from a noted orator

definitions.text: Verbal conceit from a noted orator

parts.words: Verbal conceit from a noted orator
parts.note: a conceit is a fanciful turn of phrase; read cryptically, a noted orator is a well-known figure, and what comes from him is his speech

explanation.surface: A clever rhetorical flourish delivered by a famous public speaker.
explanation.definitionFit: Metaphor and simile are examples: a word used beyond its literal sense, which is what a verbal conceit is.

clue.text: In Genoa they give a solemn assurance

indicators.note: In says the letters sit inside the words Genoa they, across the gap between them

explanation.surface: People in the Italian port of Genoa offer a solemn promise.
explanation.definitionFit: A sworn promise, as made in court, is a solemn assurance.

clue.text: Florence soaks broccoli sprouts

parts.note: Flo is the usual short form of the name Florence
to ret flax is to soak it, so rets means soaks

explanation.surface: A woman named Florence leaves broccoli to soak in water.
explanation.definitionFit: The small flower heads of broccoli or cauliflower are its sprouts in the clue's sense.

clue.text: An army awarded the MC

explanation.surface: Some military force is given the Military Cross.
explanation.walkthrough: MC looks like the Military Cross, as 'awarded' suggests; here it is a master of ceremonies.
explanation.definitionFit: A great multitude, especially an army, as in 'the heavenly host'; also the presenter of a show, a master of ceremonies.

clue.text: Laughing loudly while honking the horn

explanation.surface: A driver guffaws while sounding the car horn.
explanation.definitionFit: Hoots of laughter are loud guffaws, and a car horn hoots when sounded.

clue.text: Without doubt a South Yorkshire river

parts.note: S is the compass abbreviation for south
the Ure is a river in Yorkshire, northern England

explanation.surface: Someone identifies a river in South Yorkshire with confidence.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads 'South Yorkshire' as a county; split it into S for South and the Yorkshire river URE.
explanation.definitionFit: Being certain means having no doubt about something.

clue.text: Umpire enters with due deference to make an introduction

indicators.note: enters says the umpire's word goes inside the other piece

parts.note: pace, from Latin, means with all respect to someone, used before naming them politely
a referee, or ref, officiates like an umpire

explanation.surface: An umpire comes onto the field respectfully to open proceedings.
explanation.definitionFit: The opening section of a book that introduces it to the reader.

clue.text: Labourer has dined on quail, that's for certain

definitions.text: Labourer has dined on quail, that's for certain

parts.words: Labourer has dined on quail, that's for certain
parts.note: a labourer is a hand; once he has eaten a quail, the hand has a small game bird in it, and the phrase is a proverb about a sure thing

explanation.surface: A workman has certainly eaten a quail for dinner.
explanation.walkthrough: The proverb says one sure thing is worth more than two in the bush, so the phrase stands for a certainty.
explanation.definitionFit: The proverb prizes what one already holds securely over uncertain prospects, so it means something certain.

clue.text: Privy Councillor pro claiming the integrity of Toryism

parts.note: the Tories are the political right, so Toryism is the right
integrity is honour
a pro is skilled or capable, which is to be able

explanation.surface: A professional claims the Tory party has integrity.
explanation.walkthrough: The pieces come in reverse of the clue's order; 'claiming' and 'of' only link them.
explanation.definitionFit: Members of the Privy Council, the monarch's formal advisers, are styled by this title.

clue.text: Section of the Spanish Armada suffering damage

indicators.note: Section of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Part of the 1588 Spanish fleet takes a battering.
explanation.definitionFit: Damage or injury done to someone is what they suffer; the definition reads as a noun phrase, damage suffered.

clue.text: Money owed by one in financial straits

indicators.note: in says the one goes inside the word for financial trouble

parts.note: being in debt is to be in financial straits
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Someone short of cash has an amount owing.
explanation.definitionFit: An entry on an account recording a sum that is owed.

clue.text: Top-class artist upset by song

indicators.note: upset says the whole run of letters is turned the other way round

parts.note: A1 means first-rate, written AI in crosswords
RA is a Royal Academician, a crossword artist

explanation.surface: A leading performer is disturbed by a piece of music.
explanation.definitionFit: A solo song in an opera.

clue.text: It's quite impossible to be without a road

explanation.surface: Someone declares that having no road makes things impossible.
explanation.definitionFit: An emphatic refusal meaning never, and literally lacking any path or route.

clue.text: Walked back last month to Pennsylvania

parts.note: PA is the postal abbreviation for Pennsylvania

indicators.note: back says the month's short form is read in reverse

parts.note: Dec is short for December, the last month of the year

explanation.surface: Someone returned on foot to Pennsylvania in December.
explanation.definitionFit: To go at a steady rate on foot, step by step, is to walk.

clue.text: Lawless call for American take-over of Brazilian city

parts.note: Rio de Janeiro is a city in Brazil
a demand that one place be handed over is phrased as 'that place to us'
US is the United States, so American

explanation.surface: A demand that Americans seize a city in Brazil.
explanation.walkthrough: The call is the slogan 'Rio to US!', demanding the city be handed to America.
explanation.definitionFit: Unruly and disorderly, like a crowd running wild without regard for law.

clue.text: Stone fireplace with nickel interior

indicators.note: interior says the metal goes inside the fireplace word

parts.note: a grate is the metal frame of a fireplace
Ni is the chemical symbol for nickel

explanation.surface: A stone hearth with nickel fittings inside.
explanation.definitionFit: A hard igneous rock used for building and worktops, a kind of stone.

clue.text: Diane heads personnel on the female side

indicators.note: heads says the woman's name comes in front of the other piece

parts.note: Di is a short form of Diane
personnel are the staff of an organisation

explanation.surface: Diane leads the staff on the women's side.
explanation.definitionFit: The maternal line of a family is called this side, from the spindle used in spinning, women's work.

clue.text: Fed up with being exploited and rendered ineffective

indicators.note: in a down clue up says the word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: taken as written
to be exploited is to be used

explanation.surface: Someone fed up with being exploited loses all their fight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fed up' looks like one phrase; split it, turning FED upwards to make DEF.
explanation.definitionFit: A bomb made harmless has had its fuse removed; figuratively, a tense situation calmed.

clue.text: Party dissension featured in dramatised documentary

explanation.surface: Political disagreement is shown in a docudrama.
explanation.definitionFit: A dissenting group within a political party; strife within a group; and a blend of fact and fiction on screen.

clue.text: He has doubts about being in a corrupt environment

indicators.note: being in says the abbreviation for about sits inside the other word

parts.note: septic means infected or putrid, so corrupt
c is short for circa, Latin for about

explanation.surface: A man feels uneasy about living in a corrupt setting.
explanation.definitionFit: A doubter who questions accepted beliefs.

clue.text: Cheered and thus given a dash of spirit

parts.note: so means thus, as in 'do it so'
a drink laced with brandy has had a dash of spirit added

explanation.surface: Someone is cheered up by a drink with a nip of spirit added.
explanation.definitionFit: Comforted in distress, so cheered.

clue.text: Boasted about daughter being mobbed

indicators.note: about says the boasting word goes around the abbreviation

parts.note: to crow is to boast, so crowed
d is the genealogical abbreviation for daughter

explanation.surface: A parent bragged about their daughter being swarmed by fans.
explanation.definitionFit: A place packed with people is thronged, as if mobbed.

clue.text: Contract required for foreign and Roman law

parts.note: F is an abbreviation for foreign
lex is the Latin word for law

explanation.surface: A deal needs to satisfy both overseas and ancient Roman law.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Contract' looks like a noun, an agreement; here it is the verb, to tense a muscle.
explanation.definitionFit: To tighten a muscle by bending, as a bodybuilder does.

clue.text: Termagant initially spiteful and unfeeling

indicators.note: initially says only the first letter of spiteful is taken

parts.note: cold means without warmth of feeling

explanation.surface: A shrew who is spiteful and heartless from the start.
explanation.definitionFit: A termagant is a nagging, quarrelsome woman, a shrew.

clue.text: Japanese philosophy followed by old Stoic sage

parts.note: Zen is the school of Buddhism strongly associated with Japan

explanation.surface: Eastern thought is followed by an ancient philosopher.
explanation.definitionFit: Zeno of Citium founded the Stoic school of philosophy in Athens.

clue.text: Nick makes a really good buy

explanation.surface: Nick's purchase is a bargain.
explanation.definitionFit: A small cut made with scissors; also, in British slang, a bargain.

clue.text: Sign which should appeal to the male sex

parts.note: O is the cry of appeal, as in 'O Lord'
men are the male sex

explanation.surface: A signal designed to attract men.
explanation.walkthrough: Read 'appeal to the male sex' as the cry 'O men!'.
explanation.definitionFit: A portent or sign of what is to come.

clue.text: Subordinate has a brief moment of power

parts.note: a second is a brief moment
someone in command holds power

explanation.surface: A junior gets a short taste of authority.
explanation.definitionFit: A deputy ranks just below the leader, so is a subordinate.

clue.text: Turn around in the drive

explanation.surface: A car turns in a driveway.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Drive' looks like a driveway; it is a short outing in a car.
explanation.definitionFit: To rotate rapidly; also a brief pleasure trip in a car.

clue.text: Exposed debt-collector going back into action

indicators.note: into says the reversed piece goes inside the action word

parts.note: a deed is an action

indicators.note: going back says the debt-collector word is read in reverse

parts.note: a dun is someone who demands payment of a debt

explanation.surface: A bailiff is shown up when he returns to work.
explanation.walkthrough: 'going back' turns DUN into NUD, which 'into' puts inside DEED.
explanation.definitionFit: Stripped bare, so laid open and exposed.
